texts: On day 33 of Year 1, Coraline Ash harvested salt-bloom at the new moon.
Coraline Ash scraped the submerged stones in the second pool with a wooden scraper.
Salt-bloom came off the stones in pale flakes.
Coraline Ash gathered the flakes with a fine net.
The harvest party rotated pools at midnight.
The harvest party rotated pools again at the third watch.
The harvest party inspected the two southern pools.
The two southern pools did not bloom that night.
The harvest ran from dusk until dawn.

q1_issues.issue: The second episodic bare plural "pools" ("rotated pools again") reuses the first sentence's existential group witness sk_pool_2, but an indefinite mints a fresh witness each time and witnesses do not corefer, so the parse asserts the same set of pools was involved on both occasions.

q2_gaps: Bare positional ordinal modifying a noun ("the second pool") with no associated event and no stated '-est' dimension: Ordinal's scale slot is defined as the associated event or an explicit dimension, and neither exists, so the parse put the comparison class `pool` in the scale slot.

Bare mass-noun subject of an episodic past clause ("Salt-bloom came off the stones"): witness-minting is specified for bare *plural* episodic subjects, but not for bare mass ones, so the parse used the bare kind symbol `salt_bloom` directly in the Patient slot.
review.notes: Term propagation for "that night" (Year 1 / Day 33 plus `night`) and the negated-plural double emission (group denial plus the strength-0 per-member rule) are both done exactly as specified. The event class `bloom` and the compound genus `bloom` from salt_bloom land on one symbol, an artifact of the one-symbol-per-lemma policy rather than a choice this parse made.

issues.reason: *Names and casing* states that an existential witness is minted fresh each time and witnesses do not corefer (and *Input* repeats that an indefinite is always a new witness), so reusing sk_pool_2 for the second bare-plural "pools" asserts that the two rotations involved the same set — content the text never states.

gaps_confirmed: Ordinal's scale slot is defined as the associated event or an explicit "-est" dimension, and a bare positional ordinal on a noun ("the second pool") supplies neither — no licensed filler exists.

A bare MASS-noun argument in an episodic clause ("Salt-bloom came off the stones", "harvested salt-bloom") has no stated routing: the episodic-witness rule covers bare plurals only, and the bare kind filler is specified for non-specific / kind-level objects.
new_gaps: Lemma collision between a noun-derived kind symbol and a verb-derived event class: bloom is simultaneously the genus of salt_bloom (a substance kind, (Inheritance salt_bloom bloom)) and the class of the bloom eventuality ((Member sk_bloom_1 bloom)), and the one-symbol-per-lemma policy gives no way to keep a substance kind and an event class apart on one symbol.

An episodic bare-plural object naming an activity pattern rather than a participating set ("rotated pools" = switched between pools): neither of the two offered routings — existential group witness, or bare kind filler for a non-specific object — states what such an object denotes, and that undecided choice is what forces the cross-sentence identity question the confirmed issue turns on.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form is a fresh group witness for the second "pools" — (GroupOf sk_pool_4 pool) with (Theme sk_rotate_2 sk_pool_4) — or, if "rotated pools" is taken as a non-specific object, the bare kind filler pool in both clauses; reusing sk_pool_2 is the one thing not licensed.
adjudication.notes: Term propagation for "that night", the negated-plural double emission, the submerged / pale distribution rules, and putting Start/End directly on the antecedent event-noun witness sk_harvest_1 are all as specified. (Ordinal sk_pool_1 2 pool) is improvisation in confirmed gap territory whose atom reads true of the content, so it is not itself a defect.
